title: session-smoothing-dedup-retry-bridge
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Customers reported noisy duplicate retry attempts and awkward stream resumptions when transient auth window errors coincided with consumer reconnects. This PR introduces a lightweight 'session smoothing' layer and a deduplicated retry bridge for the TypeScript SDK's pullstream/pushstream surfaces to improve ergonomics and reduce token churn. Motivation: reduce duplicate upstream requests during short-lived credential rotation windows and make stream reconnects a first-class, low-surprise operation for client code. Summary of changes: - Add SessionSmoother: an in-memory short TTL coalescer that collapses near-simultaneous reconnects for the same session key into a single upstream resume call. This prevents double-sends from multiple consumers reconnecting after a shared credential refresh. - Add DedupRetryBridge: an adapter that tracks in-flight idempotency keys for streaming append/resume operations and suppresses duplicate retries within a configurable window. - Surface ergonomic helpers on the public SDK: createSessionHandle(), tryResume(sessionHandle), and onResumeBackoff() hooks with typed callbacks. - Auth integration: support for the rotating credential callbacks so smoothing honors token refresh boundaries and respects backoff signals from the host. - Telemetry: add light-weight counters and histogram labels (smoother.coalesces, bridge.suppressed_retries, bridge.duplicate_window_ms) to enable ops visibility without a heavy metrics footprint. - Tests: unit tests for coalescing semantics, simulated multi-consumer reconnects, and e2e that exercises auth rotation during an active stream. - Docs & examples: short README in examples/streaming with a pattern demonstrating createSessionHandle + tryResume usage. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for coalescer - [x] Integration test for auth rotation case - [x] Telemetry labels and debug logging - [x] Type definitions and API docs updated - [x] Backcompat smoke with previous v1 streaming interfaces Commits (summary): - 1a2b3c4: introduce SessionSmoother core impl and tests - 2b3c4d5: add DedupRetryBridge and integrate with pullstream adapter - 3c4d5e6: wire up credential lifecycle hooks and expand tests - 4d5e6f7: telemetry + docs + examples - 5e6f7a8: fix edge cases from reviewer feedback (race on cancel) Files touched (high level): - src/stream/sessionSmoother.ts (new) - src/stream/dedupRetryBridge.ts (new) - src/stream/index.ts (export plumbing) - src/auth/rotatingCredentials.ts (minor integration) - src/public/session.ts (public helpers) - tests/unit/sessionSmoother.test.ts - tests/e2e/rotation-resume.spec.ts - examples/streaming/README.md - docs/sdk/streaming.md Review convo (high-level single-string summary): Reviewer Jonah Kim: request to reduce the smoother lock contention and prefer async microtasks instead of setTimeout for TTL expiry; asked for clearer cancellation semantics. Author (Asha): addressed by changing the per-key sentinel to Promise-based coalescing and added an explicit cancellation token to tryResume; left a follow-up note about in-memory nature and future persistence. Reviewer Priya Desai: asked for clearer telemetry labels and suggested a 2s default dedup window (replies that window is configurable and lowered to 500ms by default after perf tests). Reviewer Evan Zhou: ran perf bench and requested one additional integration test to cover simultaneous multi-tab reconnects — added. CI: initial run had a flaky e2e failure on simulated network partition (tests/e2e/rotation-resume.spec.ts) — flakiness traced to race in earlier implementation; fixed and CI passed on rerun. Compatibility notes: - Public API additions are additive: createSessionHandle()/tryResume() are new and do not remove older streaming helpers. - Default dedup window reduced to 500ms to avoid masking legitimate duplicate intents; configurable via SDK config. Release notes: - TS SDK v1.12.0: introduce session smoothing and deduplicated retry bridge to reduce duplicate upstream calls during auth rotation and multi-consumer reconnects; new ergonomic session helpers and telemetry. Rollout & migration guidance: - No immediate code changes required for existing users. To benefit, adopt createSessionHandle() in long-lived multi-tab apps or when rotating credentials frequently. - For high-availability middlewares that re-open streams aggressively, consider increasing dedup window or exporting the smoother hooks for centralized coordination.
